title: Improve enterprise onramp: SLA routing, GPU classification, and scaling decision flow
creator: Leah O'Connor
description:
Background: Enterprise customers frequently request Reserved/Dedicated capacity with specific SLA targets (p95 latency, sustained throughput), mixed burst needs, and preferences for GPU families. Current intake is manual and slows onboarding: sales/concierge capture requirements, engineering manually maps to GPU pools and SLO bands, and finance re-prices. We need a repeatable triage flow that reduces time-to-onboard, improves accuracy of SLA/GPU matches, and surfaces trade-offs to customers and internal stakeholders.

Problem statements:
- Repetitive manual triage: eng and concierge spend 3-8 hours per request mapping requirements to GPU families and scaling policies.
- Inconsistent SLA offers: similar workloads receive different recommended SLO bands based on who triaged.
- High back-and-forth with customers due to unclear burst allowances and fallback behavior.
- Missed cost transparency: customers don’t see how throughput/latency/gpu-class choices change price.

Goals (success criteria):
- Implement a triage rubric and automated GPU-classifier to produce an initial recommended SLA band, GPU family, reserved throughput, and suggested scaling policy within 30 minutes of intake for 80% of requests.
- Reduce manual engineering touch time per request by 60% within two months of rollout.
- Provide clear recommended fallbacks and burst allowances as part of the offer; track acceptance rate and time-to-accept.
- Surface estimated monthly cost delta for at least three viable configurations (latency-prioritized, cost-prioritized, balanced).

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Intake form enhancements - expand the current reserved-capacity intake form to capture workload fingerprint signals (avg token length, 95th-token latency budget, request concurrency, long-tail session vs stateless predictions, expected steady-state RPS vs burst RPS, data residency/SLA constraints).
2) Triage scoring engine - a lightweight rules+ML hybrid (initial rollout rules-focused) that maps fingerprint -> candidate GPU families (a100/q4, h100/q8, t4/q8), suggested reserved throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec), and SLO band (bronze/silver/gold with explicit p50/p95/p99 targets).
3) SLA routing policy - definable policy that decides whether a request should be placed into a dedicated pool, unified reserved pool, or directed to hosted with commit credits; includes recommended fallback ladders (model-variant fallback, region failover).
4) Cost estimator - simple calculator that converts candidate configs into estimated monthly commit/pricing ranges and per-token unit costs.
5) UI & concierge workflow - a single view for sales/concierge that shows recommended configs, rationale, confidence score, and quick links to create a commitment proposal and change SLO sliders for customer negotiation.

Implementation notes and phases:
- Phase 0 (Discovery, 2 weeks): catalogue recent 120 dedicated requests, annotate outcome (gpu chosen, SLA agreed, post-onboarding issues). Interview 6 solution engineers and 4 account execs.
- Phase 1 (Rubric + Intake update, 3 weeks): ship intake form fields, build deterministic rules for mapping workload signals to SLO bands and GPU families. Add telemetry hooks.
- Phase 2 (Triage service MVP, 4 weeks): implement triage scoring engine (rules first, ML later), build cost estimator service, integrate with CRM/concierge UI.
- Phase 3 (Pilot + iterate, 6 weeks): run 8 customer pilots via concierge lane, measure time-to-offer, engineer touch time, SLA acceptance rate; collect feedback and tune rules.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form enforces required fields for auto-triage for 80% of incoming requests.
- Triage service returns recommended config (gpu family, reserved throughput, SLO band, fallback ladder) and confidence score within 5 minutes for synchronous intake and within 30 minutes for async.
- Internal concierge UI displays cost delta for at least 3 configurations (latency/cost/balanced) and a link to generate a commitment proposal.
- Reduction of mean eng triage time from baseline (measured during discovery) by >=60% for requests covered by auto-triage.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-reliance on deterministic rules may misclassify edge workloads. Mitigation: surface confidence and require manual review for low-confidence cases; add a "flag for engineering review" workflow.
- Risk: Cost estimator divergence from final pricing. Mitigation: conservative estimates, include ranges and clear footnote on assumptions; finance sign-off on pricing multipliers.
- Risk: Customers misuse burst credit and hit limits. Mitigation: default safer burst policy with explicit burst windows and monitoring alerts.

Open questions (product & eng):
- Where should the triage service live (console backend vs dedicated orchestration service)?
- What minimum signal set is required to reach 80% auto-triage coverage? (Prefer to avoid requiring profiling jobs for first release.)
- How do we encode multi-model workloads (embedding + gen) into a single GPU recommendation?
- SLA rollback: can we define a frictionless downgrade path if production behavior deviates?

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Solutions / Concierge: Priya Shah (primary SME)
- Engineering: Kevin Liu (runtime lead), Sara Martinez (capacity services)
- Finance: Omar Rahman (pricing)
- Sales: Daniel Park (AE lead)
- Legal/Compliance: Tanya Singh (review for data residency clauses)

Monitoring & Metrics to track post-launch:
- Time-to-initial-offer (minutes)
- Engineering touch-hours per request
- Auto-triage coverage (% of requests fully auto-scored)
- SLA acceptance rate by customers
- Post-onboarding SLA violations and incident rate (30/90 day windows)
- Cost-estimate delta vs actual billing after 60 days

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-2: Discovery & baseline metrics
- Week 3-6: Intake + rules rollout; concierge training session
- Week 7-12: Pilot with 8 customers, weekly retros and rule updates
- Week 13: Expand to concierge+sales lane, enable self-serve for low-risk profiles

Notes on ownership and follow-ups:
- PM (owner): Leah O'Connor (product)
- Eng: implement triage service API (Sara Martinez)
acceptance_criteria: Intake form captures required workload signals and validates inputs
Triage service returns recommended GPU family, reserved throughput, SLO band, and fallback ladder with confidence score
Cost estimator shows three configuration options and monthly estimate ranges
Mean engineering touch time reduced by >=60% for auto-triaged requests
Pilot completed with at least 8 customers and documented feedback
